rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (criminal history screening)
rules.requirement: If you apply to housing funded by Boston DND or an income-restricted inclusionary unit, the provider cannot use a blanket ban on people with records and may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged convictions, juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old. If you are denied because of a conviction, ask for case-by-case review and offer evidence of rehabilitation.
rules.key_value: convictions older than 5 years may not be considered

coverage.summary: Only housing providers receiving Boston DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy; also applied to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity Affirmative Marketing Program.
required_facts_not_in_data: Whether the housing provider receives DND funding or land
Whether the unit is an income-restricted unit under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy

rules.exemptions: Does not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and/or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others; does not apply to current criminal behavior; federal or state criminal history requirements that conflict preempt the policy.
rules.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (February 2017)
rules.quoted_span:
Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or 
land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on 
a case-by-case basis.
rules.interaction: Where federal or state law imposes a conflicting criminal history requirement, the federal or state law preempts this policy.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (credit screening)
rules.requirement: Providers covered by the policy may not use your credit score to approve or deny you, and may use credit history only when you have no rental history; lack of credit history alone is not a valid reason to reject you.

coverage.summary: Only housing providers receiving Boston DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
required_facts_not_in_data: Whether the housing provider receives DND funding or land
Whether the unit is an income-restricted unit under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy

rules.citation: Boston DND Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (February 2017)
rules.quoted_span:
The lack of credit 
history, as opposed to poor credit history, is not sufficient justification to reject an applicant.

notes: Policy is a DND agreement-based tenant selection policy (Feb 2017), not an ordinance; applies only to DND-funded/land or BPDA inclusionary income-restricted units. No effective date stated; assumed in force. Credit screening rule is outside the strict scope (criminal history/source of income) and included with low confidence; reviewer may drop it.
